purpose: Prove a bare-button questionnaire laid out as a TABLE is catalogued in the application's own wording. The question is the row; the wording is the row's label cell; and every row that is NOT a question must still produce no wording at all.
targeted_defect: BUG-QUESTION-ROW-BLIND - questionContainerOf recognised only fieldset / role=group / role=radiogroup. A table-laid-out questionnaire declares none of them, so question_label came back "", the catalogue stamped the question UNVERIFIED, and its identity fell back to the DOM ordinal - while the application's own wording sat one cell away in the page.

expect_controls.why: CASE A - the row IS the question, and <th scope=row> is the DOM's own way of saying so. question_key is derived from the WORDING, not the position: a row inserted above this one must not re-identify it.

fields.name: Yes
fields.question_label: Have you used tobacco in the last 12 months?
fields.question_key: q:qrow:have you used tobacco in the last 12 months?

expect_controls.why: CASE A - the SECOND answer to the same question carries the same question, so the pair is one question and not two.

fields.name: No
fields.question_label: Have you used tobacco in the last 12 months?
fields.question_key: q:qrow:have you used tobacco in the last 12 months?

expect_controls.why: CASE A - a plain <td> label cell works too; <th scope=row> is the strongest spelling of the row header, not the only one.

fields.question_label: Have you been hospitalised in the last 5 years?
fields.question_key: q:qrow:have you been hospitalised in the last 5 years?

expect_controls.why: CONTROL, CASE B - ONE control in a row is a FIELD. Rung 8 names it from the same cell (so the cell IS being read), and question_label stays empty. If this row became a question, every table-laid-out form field in every catalogue would be renamed.
CONTROL, CASE C - a <thead> filter row holds two controls and a label cell, so it satisfies every rule except the one that matters: it is not a question.
CONTROL, CASE D - the first cell holds a control, so it is not a label cell. Without that rule this row would publish a question called 'Edit'.
CONTROL, CASE D - a control sitting IN the first cell is never labelled by its own cell.
PRECEDENCE, CASE E - a <fieldset> inside a table cell WINS. The row's wording is deliberately wrong, so a row rung that displaced <legend> fails here instead of going unnoticed.

fields.question_label: Do you hold a private pilot licence?
